description: Three envelopes with VCAs, each with a pitch CV output, driven by pairs of trigger inputs

params.text: Sets the base voltage the three CV outputs carry, -4V at fully counter-clockwise to 4V fully clockwise
Sets the attack time of all three envelopes, about 2ms at fully counter-clockwise to 8 seconds fully clockwise
Sets the decay time of all three envelopes, about 2ms at fully counter-clockwise to 8 seconds fully clockwise

inputs.text: Adds to the base voltage of the three CV outputs, one volt per volt
Sets the gain of all three VCAs, doubling for every 10V, and silences them with nothing patched
Moves the attack and decay of all three envelopes together, a doubling every 2.5V
The signal that section's envelope is applied to
Starts that section's envelope and lifts its CV output by 0.5V while it stays high
Starts that section's envelope and lifts its CV output by 0.7V while it stays high

outputs.text: The base voltage with 0.5V added while that section's first trigger is high and 0.7V while its second is, so the four combinations give four pitches
That section's input through its envelope and the gain input
The sum of every section whose own output has no cable in it; patching a cable here does not give the middle section's own signal, because that section is then left out of the sum too

notes: the maker marks this module deprecated in the manual
a section's envelope fires from the sum of its two trigger inputs, so either of them alone starts it
with nothing patched to the gain input all three VCAs are silent, because that input sets the gain outright rather than modulating a knob
the two trigger offsets on a CV output are 0.5V and 0.7V, which is six semitones and about eight and a half, not the five and seven semitones the manual names
